M54.5 - Low back pain (mechanical, work-related injury)
M25.561 - Pain in right knee (compensatory due to altered gait patterns)
Mr. Brown presents with mechanical low back pain with secondary knee pain due to
compensatory movement patterns. He demonstrates significant functional limitations and
has not responded adequately to conservative treatment over the past 3 months. The
patient shows clear indications for skilled physical therapy intervention.
1. Moderate functional disability (ODI 42%) impacting work and daily activities
2. Failed conservative treatment for 3 months with multiple interventions
3. Significant strength and mobility deficits requiring skilled intervention
4. High fear avoidance behaviors (FABQ 28/66) requiring specialized education
5. Work-related functional limitations affecting ability to perform job duties
6. Potential for functional improvement with specialized physical therapy care
7. Secondary complications (knee pain) requiring comprehensive treatment approach
Page 1 of 1 Patient: Christopher Brown DOB: 06/18/1990 MRN: MRN778899 Date: 01/22/2024
Treatment Location: Denver Physical Therapy & Rehabilitation
Frequency: 3-4 sessions per week for 8 weeks
1. Manual therapy (CPT 97140) for joint mobility and soft tissue restrictions
2. Therapeutic exercise (CPT 97110) for strength, stability, and endurance
3. Postural re-education and movement pattern training
6. Gradual return to functional activities and work duties
Return to full work duties without restrictions
Physical therapy is medically necessary for Mr. Brown due to his significant functional
limitations, failed conservative treatment, and potential for improvement with skilled
intervention. The patient's work-related injury has resulted in compensatory movement
patterns affecting multiple body regions. Without appropriate treatment, he is at risk for
developing chronic pain syndrome and permanent functional limitations. The proposed
treatment plan addresses both primary and secondary diagnoses with evidence-based
